WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Guide rail position not correctly set for the current bottle size (most common cause in SOP) and/or presence of a chipped bottle in the infeed (second most common cause). Evidence: SOP lists guide-rail mis-set as cause 1 and chipped bottles as cause 2; prior jam after a changeover supports guide-rail issue.
- Difference vs historical pattern: Current incident occurs without a reported recent changeover, whereas the only prior recorded jam followed a changeover and involved a chipped bottle. This suggests the jam may be due to an unnoticed rail mis-alignment rather than a changeover-related error.

- Production impact: Line stopped (FL-101 infeed jam alarm) until jam cleared and restart verified.

    1. Switch off power at the main isolator.  
    2. Place your personal padlock on the isolator and tag with name/date.  
    3. Attempt to start the machine to confirm it cannot run.  
    4. Wear safety shoes, safety glasses, and cut-resistant gloves.  
  Step 2: Diagnosis - Inspect  
    1. Visually confirm the machine is stopped and locked out.  
    2. Check the guide-rail position against the changeover sheet (Section 8.2) for the bottle size currently in use.  
    3. Look for any chipped or broken bottles in the infeed area.  
  Step 3: Fix - Clear jam and correct rail setting  
    1. Remove jammed bottles using cut-resistant gloves.  
    2. If guide rails are out of position, move them to the correct setting per CS-FL101 and lock them.  
    3. Remove any chipped or damaged bottles from the infeed.  
  Step 4: Verify - Restart sequence  
    1. Remove the lock only after the above steps are complete.  
    2. Restart the line at 60 bottles per minute for 2 minutes.  
    3. Observe for any further jams; if none, increase speed to normal 120 bpm.  
  Step 5: Quality - Inspect first product  
    1. Quarantine the first 20 bottles after restart.  
    2. Inspect for fill quality and glass integrity; release to bulk if acceptable.  

- Root cause fix (permanent solution): Implement a mandatory guide-rail verification step after every bottle-size changeover, documented on the changeover sheet and signed by the shift lead. Include a visual lock-position check before line start-up.

- Preventive action:  
  • Add the guide-rail check to the daily start-up checklist.  
  • Train operators on the importance of rail alignment and jam-clearing safety.  
  • Schedule a monthly audit of guide-rail lock integrity by maintenance.  

- Who to notify: Maintenance Supervisor, Shift Lead, Quality Lead, and Safety Officer.
